misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:67 - Read errors in verifySafeHtml escape as RuntimeException and skip the MojoExecutionException handling.. `verify()` catches `IOException` and rethrows it as `MojoExecutionException`, so Maven reports a clean build failure that names the file. The new `verifySafeHtml()` catches its own `IOException`s and rethrows them as `RuntimeException`, which skips that handler.

The path most likely to hit this is the English counterpart. It is derived by rewriting the path: `resources-community` becomes `resources`, and the locale suffix becomes `_en`. For any translated bundle with no matching English file at that location, `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` throws `FileNotFoundException`. The plugin then aborts on an unchecked exception instead of reporting a normal verification failure. Examples are a theme laid out differently, or `replaceAll` also rewriting `resources-community` elsewhere in the absolute path.

Fix: declare `verifySafeHtml() throws IOException` and drop the `RuntimeException` wrapping, so the existing `MojoExecutionException` path handles it. Alternatively, treat a missing English file as an empty bundle or as a reported message instead of a crash.

misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:102 - The diff-trimming logic can overlap and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.. `start` (common prefix) and `end` (common suffix) are computed independently, so `start + end` can exceed `sanitized.length()`. For example, value `` sanitizes to ``, which gives start=4 and end=5 on a string of length 7. `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` then throws. That aborts the verifier with a stack trace instead of reporting the illegal HTML. Limit the suffix loop to the characters after the prefix.

misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:124 - Choice-format normalisation hides arbitrary HTML from the sanitizer check.. For `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*` and `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, every `{n,choice,...}` block is replaced with `...` before sanitizing. Any markup inside the choice is never checked. For example, a translation `{0,choice,0#|1#x}` passes the verifier. These strings end up in emails and login pages. Instead of dropping the whole choice body, strip only the `<` comparison operators (e.g. replace `([0-9])<` with `$1 lt `) so the choice texts are still sanitized.
